quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: Can be shared by the driver and passenger
Are required for both the driver and passenger
Are not required

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for both the driver and passenger
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. A motorcycle must have passenger footrests. Good footing keeps your passenger from falling off and pulling you off too.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used in an emergency
Should be used together with the rear brake
Is unsafe to use

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used together with the rear brake
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders
Turn just your head
Turn your head, shoulders, and torso

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head
questions.explanation: Look through every turn by turning just your head. Keep your shoulders still and your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Locking your brakes can:

options.text: Be helpful in most situations
Improve steering
Cause control problems

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause control problems
questions.explanation: Locking the brakes causes control problems. If your front brake locks, release it then re-apply it right away. If you lock your rear brake when stopping on a surface with good traction, keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, you should make sure it:

options.text: Has no cracks or defects
Looks nice
Fits loosely

questions.correctAnswerText: Has no cracks or defects
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards for the best protection. It should fit snugly all the way around with no visible defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet
Lanes shift
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road ahead will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: In the center of a traffic lane, there is usually an oily strip. Motorcyclists should:

options.text: Stay away from the oil and grease buildup
Not worry about the oil and grease buildup
Find the lane with the least oil and grease buildup

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay away from the oil and grease buildup
questions.explanation: Avoid riding on oil and grease buildup. The oily strip in the center of a lane is usually about two feet wide, so you can often ride on the left or right side of it and still be in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: When making a U-turn:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time
Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip over
Use the front brake to make the motorcycle more stable

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip over
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it could cause the bike to tip over. Instead, use the rear brake to control the bike's speed during the U-turn.

questions.question: The gearshift is located:

options.text: By the left footrest
By the right footrest
By the right handle grip

questions.correctAnswerText: By the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is located in front of the left footrest. The rider uses their left foot to operate it.

questions.question: A passenger should sit:

options.text: In front of the operator
Sidesaddle
Behind the operator

questions.correctAnswerText: Behind the operator
questions.explanation: Passengers should always sit behind the operator and hold firmly onto the operator's waist, hips, or midsection. They can also hold onto handgrips if the motorcycle has them. Passengers should never sit sidesaddle.

questions.question: Why is stopping in a turn difficult?

options.text: The bike is leaning, so less grip is available for braking.
The rider is focused on the turn, not on braking.
The brakes do not work when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bike is leaning, so less grip is available for braking.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful. When the motorcycle leans into a turn, some grip is used for the turn itself. This leaves less grip available for stopping.

questions.question: What kind of gloves should you wear when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Half-fingered gloves.
Full-fingered gloves.
No gloves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Full-fingered gloves.
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip and protect your hands. Always wear full-fingered gloves made of strong, durable material.

questions.question: At an uncontrolled intersection, if you arrive at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to go.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: Why should you change gears before starting a turn?

options.text: To avoid a sudden change in power while turning.
So you can keep both hands on the handlebars during the turn.
To prevent the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: To avoid a sudden change in power while turning.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you start a turn. Shifting during a turn can suddenly change power to the rear wheel and cause a skid. If you must shift during a turn, do it smoothly to prevent skidding.

questions.question: When riding near a large truck, what should you remember?

options.text: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
You should not be able to see the truck's mirrors.
Focus on your motorcycle and do not worry about the truck's mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Stay out of blind spots, especially on large trucks. Remember: if you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right lane ends
Left lane ends
Traffic control device ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They warn you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane is ending.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Signal ahead
Crossroad ahead
Divided roadway ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They warn you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road is divided ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn
No U-turn
No right turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell you about traffic laws in that area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Do you need to wear goggles, impact-resistant glasses, or a face shield?

options.text: Yes, if your motorcycle does not have a windshield.
No, they are optional if your motorcycle does not have a windshield.
Yes, only if you are under 21 years old.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if your motorcycle does not have a windshield.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle does not have a windshield, you must wear goggles, impact-resistant glasses, or a helmet with a face shield. A full-face helmet offers the best protection, even with a windshield.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a way to control a motorcycle in a turn?

options.text: Speed up through the turn.
Slow down before turning.
Lean into the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up through the turn.
questions.explanation: To control a turn safely, slow down before you enter it. Look through the turn in the direction you want to go. Press the handlebar to lean. Gradually roll on the throttle through the turn to keep the suspension stable.

questions.question: If you wear a jacket for protection while riding in hot weather, you should:

options.text: Take frequent breaks to cool off.
Remove the jacket to stay cool in the sun.
Keep the jacket on to protect you from the heat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the jacket on to protect you from the heat.
questions.explanation: A good riding jacket protects you in a crash, no matter the weather. Jackets also protect you from dehydration in hot weather. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you from overheating.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, you should stay at least this far behind other vehicles:

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least a two-second distance behind other vehicles under normal conditions. Use a larger distance when conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance when:

options.text: It is raining.
There is light traffic.
It is sunny.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is raining.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when it takes longer to stop, when you cannot see around the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy and other vehicles may cut in front of you.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Blocks most of your vision.
Lets you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.
Can be dangerous for the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet does not limit your vision. It allows you to see as far as needed for safe riding.

questions.question: When you need to react to a hazard in the road, do not:

options.text: Avoid telling other drivers you are there.
Change your speed if needed.
Use your horn and lights or signals to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid telling other drivers you are there.
questions.explanation: Alert other drivers by using your horn, lights, and signals. Change your speed as needed and adjust your position or direction to stay safe.

questions.question: When the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing, you should:

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Go slowly and look both ways.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at a flashing railroad crossing sign. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before going. Never try to go faster than a train.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
Skip the stop line and move forward to see better.
Stop at the stop line and then proceed through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop line first. Then move forward and stop again just before entering the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road:

options.text: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
You will likely lose control of the motorcycle.
You must release the rear brake to regain control.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks on a straight road while stopping, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can usually control your motorcycle even with a locked rear wheel if it is upright and going straight.

questions.question: If another vehicle is passing you, ride in:

options.text: The left portion of the lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is safest when being passed. Staying near the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Staying far from it may make the driver return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster your body removes it.
The faster it builds up in your body.
The less it affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: The faster you drink, the faster alcohol builds up in your body. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink in an hour, alcohol will still be in your body after an hour.
